video_title: Is the COVID NBA Draft the WORST ever 👀

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: The challenges of the remote 2020 NBA Draft process
quotes.excerpt: We didn't get a chance to walk the stage or anything, so it was kind of remote.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: What was the draft? What was the draft process like since you were doing COVID? I know the workouts were different.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: We didn't get a chance to walk the stage or anything, so it was kind of remote. Kind of set up like this at wherever you was at, and then they sent out a locker with all the hats. And then whenever your name got called, it just broadcasted to you. So it was an experience. I would have liked to walk that stage, though.

quotes.social_post: Tony Allen reflects on the 2020 NBA Draft experience during the pandemic, noting that the remote process lacked the traditional stage walk and in-person atmosphere of a normal draft night.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Randolph's solitary draft workout experience during COVID
quotes.excerpt: I think I did like five workouts. They were all in one spot by myself.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: How many teams did you work out for? Did you work out with players or by yourself?

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: I did. I think I did like five workouts. They were all in one spot by myself. No, no, by myself because of COVID. They wouldn't allow us to mingle.

quotes.social_post: Zach Randolph discusses the isolation of the 2020 pre-draft process, revealing he had to conduct all five of his team workouts by himself due to COVID restrictions.

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: The competitive disadvantage of the 2020 draft workout format
quotes.excerpt: I worked out for 16 teams when I got drafted.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Yes, that's definitely a big difference because usually the players go against each other. I worked out for 16 teams when I got drafted.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: 16 teams?

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Yes, 16 teams. And not only that, it was people that were ranked ahead of him. He was in workouts that he had to prove his value.

quotes.social_post: Tony Allen highlights the competitive disadvantage of the 2020 draft class, noting that players missed out on the intense, head-to-head pre-draft workouts that defined his own experience.

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: The intense, competitive nature of pre-draft workout culture
quotes.excerpt: It's like an MMA practice. Whoever going to be the first one to walk out?

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: It's like an MMA practice. Whoever going to be the first one to walk out? You know what I'm saying? That's what them workouts felt like. So you would have loved that, trust me. That would have been right up your alley. Cats faking injuries, oh, Stu getting a little bit too much, he got that jump shot going.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Let me hear it.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Hold on, he hit that three now. Oh, you know what I'm saying? You were running into that type of scene.

quotes.social_post: Tony Allen describes pre-draft workouts as an MMA practice where players would fake injuries or try to outshine each other to prove their value to teams.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Randolph's draft night celebration during the pandemic
quotes.excerpt: I had family, family friends there, and like as soon as I got drafted, draft was over.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: So you get drafted, fam. What was the draft party? What we do on draft night? How was it? Was it a kick it? Was it a turn up?

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: No, it was a turn up. I had family, family friends there, and like as soon as I got drafted, draft was over. You know, they started turning up right away. I got a lead to Detroit the next day, so I left and they were still partying. They were still getting down.

quotes.social_post: Zach Randolph shares his draft night experience, noting that while he had to leave for Detroit the next day, his family kept the celebration going after he was selected.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: The realization that the real work begins after being drafted
quotes.excerpt: Everything you done before the NBA don't really matter no more.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: What was that feeling like just hearing your name called?

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: No, it was a great feeling. It was like, man, obviously it's what you work so hard for. And something in me was just like, you know, I know it's just like the work is just beginning. Everything you done before the NBA don't really matter no more. So I was like, all right, it's about to get serious.

quotes.social_post: Zach Randolph on the moment he got drafted: It was a great feeling, but I knew the work was just beginning. Everything you did before the NBA does not really matter anymore.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Randolph's 'Welcome to the NBA' moment in training camp
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I got my welcome to NBA moment in training camp.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: I feel like I got my welcome to NBA moment in training camp. We doing drills, like one-on-one drills. I'm going against Blake Griffin, Jeremy Grant, and Mason Plumlee. And yeah, they was kicking my butt. And then I went back to the hotel that night and I'm like, damn, I don't know if I'm like, if I'm good enough, the way they made me felt that day. But I just stuck with it and just, you know, kept showing up every day.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: And that's what I was trying to ask, like far as being a professional.

quotes.social_post: Zach Randolph recalls his welcome to the NBA moment in training camp, admitting that getting dominated by Blake Griffin and others made him question if he was good enough to play in the league.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: The transition to professional habits and nutrition in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Obviously when you get in, you young, you eating a bunch of, you know, a bunch of BS.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Did you pay attention to a lot of that stuff?

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Oh yeah, no, most definitely. I mean obviously when you get in, you young, you eating a bunch of, you know, a bunch of BS and you know, just doing everything you can so you feels good as possible when 7:00 p.m. comes.

quotes.social_post: Zach Randolph talks about the transition to professional habits, noting that young players often start out eating junk before realizing the importance of nutrition to perform at 7 p.m.

quotes.speaker: Zach Randolph
quotes.summary_phrase: Reflecting on the rebuilding process in Detroit
quotes.excerpt: We lost like 28 games in a row one year, only won 14 games.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: How did you like that your time in Detroit?

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: It was a great time. It was a great time and, you know, obviously I got to Detroit when we was at the bottom and, you know, we're building. We lost like 28 games in a row one year, only won 14 games, and then, you know, we stuck it out. Took five years to, you know, finally win in the league, you know, get to the, get to the offs and, you know, we did that back-to-back years.

quotes.social_post: Zach Randolph reflects on his time in Detroit, detailing the struggle of the rebuilding years, including a 28-game losing streak, before finally reaching the playoffs.
